svg.title: T15.4_DC_synthesis_flow_decoders
svg.text: T15.4 Design Compiler Synthesis Flow for Decoders
Synthesis turns RTL into a technology-mapped netlist, then reports timing, area, power and structural risks.

text.tspan: filelist, top module, decoder family, libraries,
clock, reset, input/output delay, false paths,
unmapped cells, DRC and netlist handoff.

Tool boundary: if dc_shell is not installed, only the script skeleton and report interpretation can be verified locally. Protocol vectors do not drive synthesis, but post-synthesis sanity and sign-off reports must link back to T15.1-T15.3 evidence.
missing engine file, duplicate package, wrong top
async reset assumption, missing generated clock
flattening breaks debug, over-optimizing trace, memory wrapper mismatch
negative slack, large area, high power, unmapped cells
ACS/branch metric, alpha-beta recursion, interleaver address
check max delay and pipeline candidates
check-node min tree, layered message RAM mux, bank conflict logic
separate combinational tree from memory path
BG/Zc schedule or CBG control errors
SCL sorter, path-metric update, lazy-copy mux, CRC selector
inspect sorter depth and list-size scaling
dispatcher, soft-buffer key compare, DMA arbitration, IRQ/status fan-in
split data path and control path reports

Read order: RTL inputs -> DC setup -> constraints -> compile -> reports -> triage -> verification handoff. A timing report is not a functional proof: failing or passing synthesis must be tied back to regression, coverage and known protocol-derived parameters.
